summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of migraines, pseudotumor cerebri, hypertension, and diabetes was admitted for a severe left-sided headache accompanied by photophobia, nausea, and vomiting, lasting one week. She presented with markedly elevated blood pressure (197/122 mmHg) and a history of home BP readings up to 202/121. A CT head was normal, and lumbar puncture revealed high opening pressure, consistent with pseudotumor cerebri. She experienced transient left lower quadrant pain during the procedure, but CT abdomen/pelvis showed no acute pathology. Her headache improved with treatment, including IV morphine transitioned to oral oxycodone, IV fluids, and anti-nausea medications. Elevated liver enzymes were attributed to excessive acetaminophen intake from concurrent Percocet and Tylenol use; she was counseled on safe dosing and liver values improved. Blood pressure was managed by adjusting medications, holding several agents due to hypotension, and providing a structured restart plan. She was restarted on topiramate and acetazolamide for headache prevention and discharged home in stable, improved condition with detailed instructions on medication management, warning signs, and follow-up.
